apple_incremental_game.text: up: on the publisher's 4-CPU grader, cases using ~15–30 s CPU scored 0 and deadline-based solvers got half the CPU; size needs regrading or new runs

arc_compiler_runtime.text: up: the fix only documents the required interface, so its effect depends on how agents respond; measurable only by new runs

borden_source_inversion.text: scale ×100/109 applied with published rounding uncertainty; up for good-faith fits once the convention is documented (24 raw points for a one-shot fit; less for agents that iterate on the grader's feedback)

cta_risk_budget_optimization.text: v2.1 (shipped): up to the 5-point overseas-ratio component (4 of 80 raw) in either direction; three native paired runs through the original eval_cmd (58.75→53.75, 66.25→71.25). Historical FX-only proof applies to the previous denominator.

equivalence_class_divide_and_conquer.text: down, only for outputs inside the acceptance window; at most 9.67 points if every large official input falls in it

exchange_core_throughput.text: down: incorrect engines can get full credit

ffmpeg_swscale_reimplementation.text: down: incomplete libraries over-credited (18.9 points shown)

git_rewrite_in_zig.text: up, only for runs the original zeroed for a leftover build file or a git call in src/ (up to the whole run's score); how often real runs tripped a check is unknown

graph_node_classification.text: either: a good-faith run whose prediction file is keyed by integer node IDs scores 0 under the original verifier and moves up under the fix (neighbor_intkeys: 0 to 24.089 of 100); a run that violates the output contract (non-numeric or missing predictions, or keys that collide under str()) was scored by the original and moves down, and under best-so-far selection the added variance can raise a run's score (a general lemma); none of the real runs regraded was integer-keyed, and no gain for a real solver was established

grid_turing_robot.text: up: on the publisher's 4-CPU grader, solutions using ~15–30 s CPU per case were voided and deadline-based solvers got half the CPU; size needs regrading or new runs

integer_compression_codec.text: either: raw results were understated by a factor that depends on the submission (2.4 and 3.7 for two real submissions, 7–9 for a simple correct codec), and the fixed 0–100 scale runs from the starter (1.0) to the formula maximum (320); a real run's recorded best, 75.72, becomes 53.95 for its best submission on the fixed grader (second regrade of all 37 submissions; the first regrade of the recorded best submission alone gave 66.31 on the original grader and 50.08 on the fixed one)

jagua_nesting_optimization.text: either: down for layouts with overlaps and for forbidden rotations; up only in the constructed swim_cr leniency case, where the original's edge-crossing test rejects a near-touching layout that the fixed area test accepts (seed_shift_wrongdeg: 0 → 0.186857 raw); unchanged for valid layouts

juliet_vulnerability_analyzer.text: up, only for submissions that report CWE-78 findings with source = sink and trace [sink], the form of all 38 public answers: +600/241 = 2.49 for complete detection with every other trace accepted (measured 97.51 → 100.00), +15.00 for a CWE-78-only analyzer (measured 45.66 → 60.66); at most 6380/241 ≈ 26.473029 (conservatively bounded by 26.474) when the change lifts trace quality across the 0.60 cap (exact, from score.py:163-176; computed, not run)

lean_analysis_proofs.text: either: scored set changes from 2901 to 2338 targets

molecular_self_assembly.text: up: on the publisher's 4-CPU grader, cases using ~15–30 s CPU scored 0 and deadline-based solvers got half the CPU; size needs regrading or new runs

openrct2_theme_park_ai.text: either: the game is scored after about 68 game days instead of the promised ~4 years

openttd_transport_ai.text: up: prompt-following scripts die at the named call

order_addition_permutation_optimization.text: up: later improvements ignored when the run keeps its best by pass rate; seen in a real run (3.79 kept instead of 41.24)

pfr_formalization.text: up, new runs only: rule arithmetic allows 1.18 points for five targets and at most 2.13 with four downstream targets. The actual five targets were not proved; component controls and inferred upstream dependencies support only a conditional limit, not measured recovery.

portfolio_risk_calibration.basis: restricted decimal sweep, not a global bound
portfolio_risk_calibration.text: Sensitivity assumption only: +0.3921 / −0.10 from a finite sweep at N=242/243, strategy return −30% to +100%; largest sampled joint rise 0.3913. No proved bound for all valid submissions.

rust_multicrate_reconstruction.text: up: two packages' hidden tests do not compile and score 0 for every run that leaves the tests unchanged (cas-search 12 points, cas-cli 10); stopping at the first failing test file can cost up to 7.22 more; total at most 29.22 (28.42 when cas-mux crashes, as it did for every complete solution measured); measured +20.71 for a complete solution (73.99 to 94.70) in the publisher's inferred grading environment (the original grader plus four restored library files, which reproduces the publisher's starter score exactly); down by at most 0.10 from the stricter exemption

schemathesis_config_modernization.text: either: one weak test item; a wrapper loses up to 0.625 points and a partly passing correct decorator gains up to 0.625

schemathesis_reporting_observability.text: either: two weak test items; a submission can lose up to 4.76 points (wrong report writer and wrong coverage output); good-faith work can gain up to 2.76 (a correct report writer whose suite has another name, plus coverage tests), and a rise reaches 4.76 only if a submission makes the `GeneratedValue` class that the original coverage tests import unimportable, so 4.76 is used as the bound in both directions

treant_forest.text: Scale interval from rounded average, allowing zero-score clipping and second-segment runs; no exact inversion from the public mean.

tree_block_partitioning.text: up, only for programs that multiply a value by itself in place (`v *= v`)

triangulation_coloring_optimization.text: either: a different flip rule; plus up for solutions voided by the CPU share on the publisher's 4-CPU grader, and deadline-based solvers got about half a CPU

vibrating_path_graph_coloring.text: up: on the publisher's 4-CPU grader, solutions using ~14–30 s CPU per case got no score and deadline-based solvers got half the CPU; size needs regrading or new runs

warehouse_forklift_routing.text: up: runs over 60 s on any input, or over about 30 s of CPU per input on the publisher's 4-CPU grader, were voided, and deadline-based solvers got about half a CPU; ceiling ≈30.6 (30.3 before display rounding)
